node_kinds.name: PTD_Principal
node_kinds.description: Anything that can hold privilege: a user, a role, a service account, or an external system that decides on their behalf.

node_kinds.name: PTD_Action
node_kinds.description: An operation a principal may be allowed to perform, as the policy names it.

node_kinds.name: PTD_Resource
node_kinds.description: What an action is performed on, named by the document a decision turned out to allow.

node_kinds.name: PTD_Attribute
node_kinds.description: A field a decision depends on, whether it was read from data or believed from an external answer. It is what an escalation aims at.

node_kinds.name: PTD_Rule
node_kinds.description: A rule of the analyzed policy. Whether the PEP asks for it directly is the is_decision property.

relationship_kinds.name: PTD_CanPerform
relationship_kinds.description: The principal can get this out of a decision, given the data as it stands. The condition property is what still has to hold.

relationship_kinds.name: PTD_Reads
relationship_kinds.description: The rule depends on this attribute. A dependency, not a capability, which is why it is not traversable.

relationship_kinds.name: PTD_WrittenBy
relationship_kinds.description: The attribute can be written by this principal. It describes the system around OPA and is declared rather than derived from any policy.

relationship_kinds.name: PTD_CanEscalateTo
relationship_kinds.description: The principal can reach the position the other one holds, by writing something they are allowed to write. The only edge that means privilege escalation.

relationship_kinds.name: PTD_TaintedBy
relationship_kinds.description: The value comes from this external source rather than from the policy. A dependency, not a capability.
